title: Labeling cleanup playbook — personal scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad — Data cleanup & labeling edge cases (working notes)

Purpose:
- Capture quick heuristics and example-driven rules while I iterate on the formal labeler guide.
- Surface recurring ambiguous cases from the small-batch QA passes last month.
- Keep a list of sample inputs to use in the evaluation harness and the rule-based cleanup script.

Context / background:
- Running cleanup on 120k samples from the early prod ingestion pipeline (mostly user prompts + model responses).
- Focus areas: noise removal, PII detection & redaction, multi-intent prompts, partial answers, code blocks, and formatting artifacts from scraped sources.
- Downstream consumers: evals team (quality checks), embeddings pipeline (needs consistent text), privacy team (PII tagging).

Goals for this doc (short-term):
1) Enumerate edge cases we keep hitting.
2) Propose a minimal label taxonomy for manual review.
3) Draft directives for automated cleanup scripts (regex + heuristics).
4) Collect canonical examples (raw -> cleaned -> label) for unit tests.

Quick labeling taxonomy (proposed minimal):
- keep: content is usable as-is, minor whitespace fixes allowed
- edit: content requires non-destructive edits (remove tracking IDs, normalize bullets, fix obvious markdown leakage)
- redact-pii: contains PII that must be removed or tokenized (SSN, full credit card numbers, private keys)
- drop: content should be excluded from dataset (pornographic, extremist incitement, machine-generated spam)
- split: multiple independent prompts/responses in a single sample; should be split into N records
- ambiguous: reviewer unsure; needs domain reviewer or policy check
- code-only: contains code (should be routed to code pipeline/skip for text models)

Top recurring edge cases + suggested actions:
1) Mixed instructions + metadata headers
   Example: "# Instruction
Answer briefly.
SystemID: 1234ab
What is the capital of France?"
   Action: drop metadata lines matching ^(SystemID|SourceID|exported_at): and label as edit if content remains. If header contains PII, mark redact-pii.

2) Partial-chat concatenation (two or more conversations concatenated without delimiter)
   Example: "A: hi
B: hello
A: what's the weather?
B: ... (then later)
Customer: how do I reset?
Agent: ..."
   Action: heuristic: if two roles repeat and there is a sudden new role token (Customer/CustomerSupport) treat as split. Otherwise label ambiguous for manual.

3) Long chains of short boilerplate (ratings, surveys)
   Example: "Rate from 1-5: 4
Comments: none
Rate from 1-5: 3
Comments: good"
   Action: compress repeated survey noise into a single compact representation (or drop if downstream doesn't need surveys). Label as edit.

4) Embedded CODE + natural language explanation
   Example: triple-backtick blocks with private keys or config
   Action: If code block contains private keys or creds (regex detect: PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY), label redact-pii and remove. If code-only and useful for code LLMs, mark code-only; otherwise drop from text pipeline.

5) Non-English fragments in an otherwise English corpus (one-off words, quotes)
   Action: preserve short foreign tokens (<=10 chars) unless entire sample is non-English. Add language tag in metadata if >30% non-English. For ambiguous scripts (emoji-only) mark edit.

6) HTML/markdown render artifacts (\u003cdiv\u003e,  , markdown tables jammed in)
   Action: run lightweight sanitizer: unescape html entities; remove tags except pre/code; collapse repeated \n and whitespace; label edit. Keep original in audit log for traceability.

7) Toxic content with quoted context (user quoting slur to ask what it means)
   Action: if intent is explanatory or reporting, keep but flag with context tag (need policy review). If praise/endorsement of slur or violent content, drop. Mark ambiguous for reviewer when unclear.

8) Short single-word queries that are ambiguous ("help", "thanks")
   Action: keep if frequency in dataset is low; otherwise consider drop for embeddings if they add noise. Implement frequency threshold heuristic.

9) Repeated system footprints / agent signatures ("Sent from my iPhone")
   Action: strip via signature list; label edit. If signature includes email/phone -> redact-pii.

Sample labeled examples (raw -> cleaned -> label):
- raw: "My SSN is 123-45-6789, what's the tax rate?"
  cleaned: "[REDACTED_SSN] what's the tax rate?"
  label: redact-pii

- raw: "\u003ctable\u003e...\u003c/table\u003e Question: how to bake?"
  cleaned: "Question: how to bake?"
  label: edit

- raw: "\nUser: hey
Bot: hi
User: error code 500
Bot: try this
User: thanks
User: actually also need billing

User2: how to cancel?"
  cleaned: split into two samples at user2 marker
  label: split

Automation heuristics to implement (first pass):
- PII regex suite: emails, phone, credit card (Luhn), SSNs, private key markers, AWS secret-like keys.
- Signature whitelist: common footers to strip (Sent from, View in browser, __Subscribe__) but preserve when they contain user text of value.
- Split heuristics: look for role tokens (User:, Customer:, Agent:, Bot:, System:) and if a role token repeats non-consecutively, consider split candidate.
- Language detect quick-pass (langid) to tag non-english.
- Code block detection: backticks, indentation, common file extensions.
- Spam detection: very high repeat character ratio, lots of urls, single-word repetition -> drop or mark for review.

Unresolved / open questions (to decide in formal guide):
- Thresholds for frequency-based dropping (top 1% repeated queries?)
- When to keep quoted toxic content vs redaction: do we keep for robustness in safety evals?
- Exact list of PII patterns we redact vs hash (e.g., phone numbers hashed with salt?) Needs legal/privacy sign-off.
- Policy overlap with privacy team: what level of audit trail is required before dropping?

Small checklist to run during manual review pass:
- [ ] Does sample contain explicit PII? -> redact-pii
- [ ] Is it multiple distinct user interactions? -> split
- [ ] Is content primarily code? -> code-only
- [ ] Is it clearly low-value or spam? -> drop
- [ ] Any policy-sensitive language quoted for explanation? -> flag for policy review

Notes about tooling + integrations:
- Add small set of unit tests based on sample examples above to labeling-scripts repo (see linked PR context).
- Add a fast-check column in the review UI: suggested_action (keep/edit/redact/drop/split), confidence (low/med/high), rule_trigger (regex id or heuristic id).
- Store original raw text in audit bucket with a pointer in the cleaned record (audit_trace_id) for traceability; privacy flagged records get shorter retention.

Next short steps (my plan):
1) Convert these examples to JSONL for labeling-scripts unit tests (target by 2026-02-10).
2) Draft the concise labeler guide doc (1 pager) with the taxonomy above and hand to privacy for review.
3) Prototype the signature stripper + PII regex in a single preprocessing pass and run on a 10k sample for QA.

Random notes to self: keep this doc informal. Capture more oddballs during the next QA session — Samir will have the exports from the helpdesk system (ticket export #helpdesk-jan). Riley to check whether the product analytics logs have sampling bias toward short prompts.

Useful references mentioned: CONFLUENCE-DataLabeling-Cleanup-Plan (linked), JIRA-CLN-1128 (cleanup epic), PR#98 (labeling-scripts heuristics).

——END SCRATCHPAD——

(Date log: edits 2026-01-18 initial; 2026-01-25 added code block rules; 2026-02-03 added sample list and unresolved questions.)
